method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: QUOTED from Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors' (published 30 June 2026), 20 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13418215). S2: QUOTED from Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin' (published 24 February 2017), 12 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC5323428). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, evidence-based recommendations from a European expert group (COST Action BM1101) built on a structured literature review (Medline, Embase, Cochrane) and graded with the American Academy of Neurology evidence and recommendation scheme. S1 claims are unchanged. Searches for a newer society guideline (Europe PMC: cervical dystonia AND guideline/consensus/recommendations 2015-2026; botulinum AND guideline/consensus AND dystonia, open access 2018-2026) found the retired AAN 2016 guideline, the Dressler 2021 IAB consensus (dosing only in tables) and a 2026 Italian Delphi consensus whose statements are in tables; S2 was the strongest open graded source. S2's starting doses cite European summaries of product characteristics from 2012-2015.

claims.claim: **Cervical dystonia is sustained or intermittent contraction of neck muscles that forces the head into abnormal positions.** BoNT-A is first-line treatment for focal and multifocal muscle overactivity.
claims.source_text: whereas cervical dystonia is marked by sustained or intermittent contractions of neck muscles that force the head into abnormal positions … BoNT-A is widely recognized as the first-line treatment for focal and multifocal muscle overactivity, due to its favorable efficacy and safety profile compared with systemic pharmacological therapies
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First confirm isolated cervical dystonia and exclude mimics:** generalised, combined, paroxysmal or neurodegenerative dystonia, atlantoaxial subluxation, musculoskeletal disorders, cervical spine injury (traumatic, infectious or neoplastic), tics and functional dystonia.
claims.source_text: Evaluation begins with confirmation that the abnormal posturing is consistent with isolated cervical dystonia and not attributable to other conditions. The most frequent differential diagnoses of isolated cervical dystonia include alternative forms of cervical dystonia (such as cervical involvement in generalized dystonia, dystonia combined with additional movement disorders, paroxysmal dystonia, and dystonia associated with neurodegenerative diseases), as well as other conditions such as atlantoaxial subluxation, musculoskeletal disorders, cervical spine injury (traumatic, infectious, or neoplastic), and movement disorders including cervical motor tics and functional dystonia.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classify the pattern** with the classical terms (torticollis, laterocollis, anterocollis, retrocollis) and the COL-CAP system, which separates neck-driven (collis) from head-driven (caput) components.
claims.source_text: Two complementary frameworks are typically applied: the classical nomenclature (torticollis, laterocollis, anterocollis, retrocollis) and the COL-CAP (Collis-Caput) system, which distinguishes neck-driven (collis) from head-driven (caput) components.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rate severity with TWSTRS** (severity, disability, pain); the modified Tsui scale is an alternative. Also ask about anxiety, depression, pain, sleep and fatigue.
claims.source_text: The Toronto Western Spasmodic Torticollis Rating Scale (TWSTRS-1) is the primary instrument used for multidimensional evaluation of severity, disability, and pain. The modified Tsui scale may serve as an alternative or complementary motor severity measure. … It is also recommended evaluating non-motor symptoms, including anxiety, depression, pain fluctuations, sleep disturbances, and fatigue
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start BoNT-A once a clear dystonic pattern causes pain, abnormal posture, functional limitation or social impairment.** The decision rests on the dystonic driver and whether it is tonic, phasic or tremor-dominant, not just on how far the head deviates.
claims.source_text: Botulinum toxin type A should be initiated once a clearly defined dystonic pattern is established and results in pain, abnormal posture, functional limitation, or social impairment. The panel noted that treatment does not depend only on the degree of head deviation but on the identification of the dystonic driver and whether the pattern is tonic, phasic, or tremor-dominant.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Record a baseline** (pain score, range of motion, dystonic activation, tremor) to guide muscle choice and measure later cycles. The panel favours early treatment to prevent maladaptive movement and secondary musculoskeletal problems.
claims.source_text: A baseline evaluation including pain scoring, range of motion, dystonic activation, and tremor characterization is recommended to guide target selection and to allow objective assessment in subsequent cycles. … Early treatment initiation was endorsed by the clinicians, as it may prevent maladaptive motor behavior and secondary musculoskeletal complications.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Goals:** a more neutral, comfortable head posture, less pain, better daily function and less tremor. Set them individually and explain expected results.
claims.source_text: Therapeutic goals center on restoring a more neutral and comfortable head posture, reducing pain, improving functional capacity in daily activities, and diminishing dystonic tremors when present. The panel stressed the importance of individualized goal setting based on the functional impact of the dystonic pattern. Clear communication of expected outcomes is essential to align patient expectations and facilitate consistent evaluation over time.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Evidence grade:** class I evidence shows all three BoNT-A products and BoNT-B improve cervical dystonia (level A for abobotulinumtoxinA, onabotulinumtoxinA and rimabotulinumtoxinB; level B for incobotulinumtoxinA). BoNT-A also reduces dystonia pain (level A).
claims.source_text: There is class I evidence that the three BoNT-A and the BoNT-B formulations significantly improve dystonia in CD. The recommendation level is A for abobotulinumtoxinA, onabotulinumtoxinA, and rimabotulinumtoxinB, and level B for incobotulinumtoxinA … There is class I evidence that BoNT-A reduces pain symptoms in CD (level A).
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **BoNT-A and BoNT-B work equally well and for as long (level A), but BoNT-B causes more side effects (level B),** notably dry mouth and swallowing difficulty.
claims.source_text: Dry mouth and swallowing difficulties were more common with BoNT-B … Botulinum neurotoxin-A and BoNT-B have a comparable effect and duration of effect (level A). Side effects are more frequent with BoNT-B (class I evidence, level B).
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pick muscles by the direction of abnormal movement.** Rotation (torticaput/torticollis): contralateral sternocleidomastoid and semispinalis capitis; ipsilateral splenius capitis/cervicis, levator scapulae, inferior oblique of the head and trapezius.
claims.source_text: The appropriate selection of muscles to inject requires a detailed analysis of the movement pattern exhibited by the cervical muscles, identifying the vectors of abnormal movement direction and selecting the muscles thought to contribute to that pattern. This can be subclassified based on the COL-CAP concept []. According to the displacement vectors, the most commonly injected muscles would be as follows: Horizontal plane: cephalic rotation (torticaput)/cervical rotation (torticollis) Contralateral sternocleidomastoid, semispinalis capitis; Ipsilateral splenius capitis/cervicis, levator scapulae, inferior oblique of the head, trapezius.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lateral tilt (laterocaput/laterocollis):** ipsilateral sternocleidomastoid, levator scapulae, middle and posterior scalenes, trapezius, splenius and semispinalis capitis. **Extension (retrocaput/retrocollis):** bilateral splenius, semispinalis, trapezius and inferior oblique of the head.
claims.source_text: Lateral plane: cephalic lateralization (laterocaput)/cervical lateralization (laterocollis) Ipsilateral sternocleidomastoid, levator scapulae, middle and posterior scalenes, trapezius, splenius capitis/cervicis, semispinalis capitis. Anteroposterior plane: cephalic extension (retrocaput)/cervical extension (retrocollis) Bilateral splenius capitis/cervicis, semispinalis capitis/cervicis, trapezius, inferior oblique of the head.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Flexion (anterocaput/anterocollis):** bilateral sternocleidomastoids, levator scapulae, anterior scalenes, longus colli/capitis. Take care with deep anterior neck muscles because of dysphagia and airway risk.
claims.source_text: Anteroposterior plane: cephalic flexion (anterocaput)/cervical flexion (anterocollis) Bilateral sternocleidomastoids, levator scapulae, anterior scalenes, longus colli/capitis. … The physicians stressed caution when administering injections to deep anterior cervical muscles due to the elevated risk of dysphagia and airway complications.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ultrasound improves accuracy in the scalenes and deep neck flexors and extensors;** EMG helps find active motor units in tremor-dominant patterns. Guidance is not mandatory for every muscle.
claims.source_text: Ultrasound guidance improves injection accuracy in the scalene muscles and deep cervical flexor and extensor muscles, while EMG guidance may assist in tremor-dominant patterns to identify active motor units … Nevertheless, US- or EMG-guided injection should not be considered mandatory for every muscle
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **EMG-assisted muscle selection (level A):** in treatment-naive patients, choosing muscles by examination plus polymyographic EMG and injecting under EMG guidance improves dystonia and pain more than examination alone; without polymyography 24–41% of dystonic muscles were missed. It can also help when benefit wanes (level C).
claims.source_text: There is class I evidence that, in treatment-naïve patients, improvements in dystonia and pain are greater if muscles are selected based on a combination of clinical examination and pEMG and injections are performed with EMG guidance (level A) … Other studies showed that without pEMG, 24-41% of the dystonic muscles were missed, and 25-35% of the injected muscles were misjudged as dystonic … In patients with deterioration of treatment effect, the use of pEMG and EMG guidance can improve the results (class III, level C)
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Individualise the total dose** by pattern complexity, number of muscles, body build and response to past cycles. Higher doses are often needed when both caput and collis components are active or tremor is prominent.
claims.source_text: Total dosing should be individualized according to pattern complexity, number of muscles involved, patient morphology, and response to previous treatment cycles. Higher doses are often required when both caput and collis components are active or when tremor is prominent.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Working dilutions:** onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U/1 mL; incobotulinumtoxinA 100 U/1 mL; abobotulinumtoxinA 500 U/2.5 mL or 500 U/1 mL.
claims.source_text: OnabotulinumtoxinA: 100 U/1 mL; IncobotulinumtoxinA: 100 U/1 mL; AbobotulinumtoxinA: 500 U/2.5 mL or 500 U/1 mL.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reinject about every 12–16 weeks,** matching the expected duration of benefit. The panel accepts a flexible 8–12-week interval only for incobotulinumtoxinA.
claims.source_text: The typical retreatment interval is approximately 12-16 weeks, corresponding to the expected duration of clinical benefit [,]. A flexible 8-12-week interval is acceptable only for incobotulinumtoxinA
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Starting total dose per session:** abobotulinumtoxinA 500 IU (level A; an average 200–400 IU under EMG guidance also worked, with fewer side effects); incobotulinumtoxinA 120 IU (level B); rimabotulinumtoxinB 2,500 or 5,000 IU (level B) or 10,000 IU (level A). No optimal onabotulinumtoxinA starting dose can be recommended (level U); studies used 60 to 374 IU in total.
claims.source_text: An initial total dose of 500 IU abobotulinumtoxinA is effective (level A), although other dosages might be used (, ). An initial total dose of 120 IU incobotulinumtoxinA is probably effective (evidence class I, level B) (). No clear recommendations can be given on the optimal starting does of onabotulinumtoxinA (level U). An initial total dose of 2,500 or 5,000 IU rimabotulinumtoxinB (evidence class I, level B) or 10,000 IU (level A) is probably effective. … It is worth mentioning, however, that CD could be successfully treated using an average total dose of 200-400 IU abobotulinumtoxinA under electromyography (EMG) guidance, resulting also in fewer side effects … The mean total doses of original onabotulinumtoxinA injections, reported in 30 studies, as assessed by a systematic review, ranged from 60 to 374 IU in total
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **One tested split of 500 IU abobotulinumtoxinA:** 100–200 IU sternocleidomastoid, 250–350 IU splenius, 100–200 IU trapezius and 100–200 IU levator scapulae (RCT, 68 patients).
claims.source_text: An initial dose of 500 IU abobotulinumtoxinA (divided into 100-200 IU in the sternocleidomastoid muscle, 250-350 IU in the splenius, 100-200 IU in the trapezius, and 100-200 IU in the levator scapulae) significantly improved CD with respect to placebo in another RCT on 68 patients
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Switching products, dose conversion:** 1 IU onabotulinumtoxinA to 3 IU abobotulinumtoxinA (level A), though 1:2.5 may be equally safe and effective (level B); onabotulinumtoxinA to incobotulinumtoxinA 1:1 (level B).
claims.source_text: It is recommended to use a conversion of 1 IU onabotulinumtoxinA to 3 IU abobotulinumtoxinA (level A) (, ), although conversion ratios of 1:2.5 might be equally safe and effective (class I, level B) … It is recommended to use a conversion of 1:1 IU onabotulinumtoxinA to incobotulinumtoxinA (class I, level B).
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Reinjecting sooner than 12 weeks:** only incobotulinumtoxinA has class I evidence that shorter intervals do not raise antibody risk; for the other products data are insufficient (level U). Experts advise leaving reinjection as long as clinically possible to limit antibody formation; product information gives a 10- to 12-week minimum.
claims.source_text: There is only one class I study showing that, with incobotulinumtoxinA, treatment intervals <12 weeks do not increase the risk of developing antibodies. There is insufficient data to recommend or discourage the use of an interval <12 weeks for treatment with rimabotulinumtoxinB, onabotulinumtoxinA, and abobotulinumtoxinA (level U) … In a consensus statement, experts recommend that reinjection is left as long as clinically possible, to minimize the chance of antibody responses … The current manufacturer information suggest that the minimal interval between injections should be 10 (SPC onabotulinumtoxinA and incobotulinumtoxinA) to 12 weeks
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Dysphagia is the main adverse effect,** especially with deep or anterior neck injections or high doses there. Manage with diet changes, hydration and speech or swallow therapy; next time use lower doses or other targets, with US and EMG guidance.
claims.source_text: Dysphagia is the most notable adverse event in cervical dystonia, arising particularly when deep or anterior cervical muscles are injected or when doses in these regions are too high. Management includes dietary adjustments, hydration support, and temporary referral to speech or swallow therapy. For subsequent injection cycles, lower doses or alternative muscle targets should be used, and injection technique should be optimized with US and EMG guidance.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Excess weakness shows as reduced neck support or exaggerated compensatory postures;** it is usually reversible and calls for a lower dose or better targeting.
claims.source_text: More clinically significant events relate to excessive weakening of injected or adjacent muscles, which may manifest as impaired gait, diminished limb function, or, in cervical dystonia, reduced neck support or exaggerated compensatory postures. These events are usually reversible but indicate the need for dose reduction or improved muscle targeting in subsequent cycles.
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review within two to four weeks of injection** to pick up early complications and refine the plan.
claims.source_text: A structured follow-up visit within two to four weeks allows clinicians to detect early complications, refine plans
claims.locator: Mexican multidisciplinary panel of 15 specialist injectors, endorsed by COMEFYR (Hernández Franco J, Santamaría Molina, et al.), Toxins vol 18, article 287, doi 10.3390/toxins18070287, 'Botulinum Toxin Type A in Spasticity and Cervical Dystonia: Practical Clinical Recommendations from a Mexican Multidisciplinary Panel of Specialist Injectors', published 30 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13418215/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Dysphagia rates and risk:** commoner after bilateral sternocleidomastoid injections; usually mild (severe in under 5%) and gone in 2–3 weeks. Reported rates range from 3.4% (current onabotulinumtoxinA) to 19.4% (abobotulinumtoxinA), with incobotulinumtoxinA 12.6% and rimabotulinumtoxinB 15.6%. Adding ultrasound guidance may lessen recurrent dysphagia (level U).
claims.source_text: Bilateral sternocleidomastoid injections are more frequently associated with dysphagia (). Dysphagia is often mild (severe in <5% of the cases), very rarely requires hospitalization or feeding tube, and disappears gradually after 2-3 weeks (). Dysphagia is relatively common: 7.1% of the patients reported dysphagia after treatment with the original onabotulinumtoxinA, 3.4% with the new generation onabotulinumtoxinA, 19.4% with abobotulinumtoxinA, 12.6% with incobotulinumtoxinA, and 15.6% with rimabotulinumtoxinB … The additional use of ultrasound may lessen recurrent dysphagia after botulinum treatment (class IV, level U)
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid BoNT in pregnancy where possible, and during breastfeeding** (insufficient human data, level U). **Anticoagulants:** haematoma risk with coumarins seems low (level U). **Myasthenia gravis, ALS and Lambert–Eaton syndrome** are listed contraindications in product information, because BoNT can worsen or unmask them.
claims.source_text: therefore, BoNT treatment during pregnancy is not recommended and should be avoided whenever possible (class IV, level U). No studies have been conducted on the effect of BoNT on the nursing child; to exclude side effects, BoNT treatment should be avoided during lactation (class IV, level U) … The risk of hematoma following BoNT treatment by concomitant use of coumarin derivatives has not been sufficiently studied but seems low (class IV, level U) … Myasthenia gravis, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Lambert-Eaton diseases are reported as contraindications to BoNTs treatment in the respective SPCs
claims.locator: Contarino MF, Van Den Dool J, Balash Y, et al. (European expert group, COST Action BM1101), Frontiers in Neurology 8:35, doi 10.3389/fneur.2017.00035, 'Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Recommendations for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia with Botulinum Toxin', published 24 February 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5323428/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **True primary non-response is extraordinarily rare;** first re-examine the patient, the diagnosis and the injection strategy.
claims.source_text: The panel agrees that this situation is considered extraordinarily rare. When an apparent therapeutic failure is observed after an initial injection cycle, the first step is systematic clinical re-evaluation.

claims.claim: **Secondary non-response, stepwise:** reassess and review goals; optimise muscle choice and technique with guidance; test for neutralising antibodies if suspected; switch BoNT-A formulation if resistance is shown; if still inadequate, consider a washout of about 8–12 months while considering functional neurosurgery.
claims.source_text: the group recommends a stepwise management approach for both spasticity and cervical dystonia management. This includes: Comprehensive clinical reassessment and goal review; Optimization of muscle selection and injection technique, preferably with guidance methods such as US, EMG, or electrical stimulation; Consideration of laboratory evaluation for immune-mediated resistance when the pattern suggests neutralizing antibodies; If resistance is documented, switching to a different BoNT-A formulation is advised; Persistence of inadequate response despite a change in biologic may justify a washout period of approximately 8-12 months, while alternative interventions, including functional neurosurgical procedures, are considered

claims.claim: **Children:** focal cervical dystonia is uncommon, usually part of generalised or segmental dystonia, and no toxin is approved for childhood dystonia.
claims.source_text: Focal cervical dystonia is not a common condition in the pediatric population, as it is usually part of a generalized or segmental dystonic syndrome, and no toxin has approval for use in dystonic syndromes in childhood.

Neutralising antibodies are one cause, commoner with rimabotulinumtoxinB (antibody failure in 44% in one short series), and switching from BoNT-A to BoNT-B helps only temporarily (level U).
claims.source_text: Secondary non-responsiveness is defined as "insufficiently improved posture after three or more unsuccessful injection cycles in CD patient's previously achieving satisfactory results" (). claims.claim: **Oral drugs have a limited role:** trihexyphenidyl is poorly tolerated; diazepam or clonazepam mainly ease pain, anxiety and perhaps dystonic tremor; tetrabenazine is limited by depression and parkinsonism. **When BoNT is unsatisfactory,** pallidal deep brain stimulation appears a better choice than selective peripheral denervation, which is now rarely done.
claims.source_text: Oral medication has a limited role. Trihexyphenidyl is classically proposed, but the tolerance profile is low (). Benzodiazepines, especially diazepam and clonazepam, mainly reduce dystonia-related pain, anxiety, and possibly dystonic tremor (). Tetrabenazine, although possibly effective (), is limited by the frequent side effect of depression and parkinsonism. Evidence on the effectiveness of allied care treatments, including physiotherapy and cognitive behavioral therapy, is scanty (). In those with unsatisfactory botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) effect, surgery may be considered. Peripheral surgery, such as selective peripheral denervation, can provide improvement in about two-thirds of cases, with frequent relapses and is now rarely performed (, ). Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the globus pallidus pars interna appears to be a better choice, despite potential severe complications (). Alternative DBS targets, such as the subthalamic nucleus, need further investigation
